pr.body:
## Problem

Replay can wait for parent-context jobs queued behind ordinary pipeline jobs in other memory contexts. The watchdog previously observed only completions in the awaited context, so productive FIFO work could trigger a false timeout and crash recovery.

## What changes

Observe completed jobs across all memory contexts when resetting the existing monotonic no-progress deadline. Synchronization still waits for the requested context to drain. Add eight deterministic GPU-independent FIFO, progress-then-stall, normal-completion and cancellation regressions, and document the corrected timeout semantics.

Fork setup regressions observe the actual startup offer and EOF before fatal injection, retaining strict native exit, reap and crash-counter assertions. Separate closed-reader controls cover startup delivery failure.

## Why this matters

Useful replay work no longer triggers recovery merely because its completions belong to a different memory context. A worker that stops completing work still reaches its configured deadline.

## Why this approach

Read the existing counters under the existing queue mutex and widen their sum to `uint64_t`. This keeps the correction within progress accounting while preserving queue ordering, heartbeat, cancellation, recovery, CLI options, public interfaces, formats and cache-marker policy.

## Verification and limits

- Independent Linux Debug/Release x exceptions OFF/ON: all 260 registered CPU tests passed per configuration, plus 99 decisive tests repeated three times per configuration (2,228 passing candidate executions).
- Independent recovery stress: sigmask, stdout-dup2 and stdin-dup2 each passed 25 additional repetitions in both Debug and Release (150 executions), retaining all original native/counter/outcome assertions.
- Independently compiled original-rule Debug/Release controls reproduced exactly the intended two false-timeout assertions and native/counter outcomes for one and two compilation threads. All eight zero-completion stall and normal-success controls passed. Candidate progress-then-stall assertions remain unchanged and passed throughout the matrix.
- The current base includes [worker-reason reporting from #73](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/pull/73). The decisive selection covers rich/legacy events, native outcomes, retry, fork, cancellation and header/CLI compatibility together with the watchdog regressions.
- A separate fresh final checker passed all 99 decisive tests three times in both Debug and Release (594 executions), with no findings.
- [Independent work-unit report](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/harness-artifacts/runs/issue-70/issue70-integrate73-20261103/reports/check-unit-3.json) and [separate final report](https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/blob/harness-artifacts/runs/issue-70/issue70-integrate73-20261103/reports/check-final-2.json).
- Native Windows execution was explicitly waived as unavailable on this machine and remains unverified. These CPU fixtures establish no GPU, driver, Steam timing or output-durability result.

## Task references

Closes https://github.com/robinwassen/Fossilize/issues/70
